_doc: Simulated narrators for pipeline testing (scripts/simulation/simulate_sessions.py).
These are NOT participants: every log they produce is flagged simulated.
order: story + condition in play order, '+' = animations on, '-' = baseline (balanced with P1, P2, P10, P16).
reference: real sessions whose register the child model imitates (never the same story).
Traits are per-recording probabilities unless noted. Anchors measured on the real sessions:
P1 (7, dis)  8 words/recording, grammar error 14%, content error 43%, corrections resolved 52% with animations, 14% spoken over the animation
P2 (8, dis)  adult prompts in 57% of recordings, grammar error 68%, content error 74%
P10 (8, dis) adult prompts in 71%, one-word answers, 44% spoken over the animation
P16 (11, dis) 9 words/recording, grammar error 2%, richer vocabulary (type/token .36 vs .22 for P1)
self = self-reported dyslexia: oral level slightly above the diagnosed children of the same age.
len_med: median words spoken by the child per recording. turns_*: mean recordings per scene.
uptake_*: probability that the child acts on an animation it has seen (an ASSUMPTION, not a finding).
p_name: probability that such a reaction to the Silhouette animation is a name (the real children never gave one).
asr: what the recogniser and push-to-talk do to a recording: a mis-heard word, a missed start (clip_head) or end (clip_tail),
no final full stop, lower-case start. Anchors: no final stop in 20% (P1), 32% (P10), 12% (P2), 4% (P16) of recordings.
grammar / disfluency: the patterns this child keeps for the whole session (keys in child.py); grammar_rare: once per session at most.
len_max: longest recording of the child alone, in words (weak narrators do not produce long clean sentences).
Each child's own words and habits (labels, fillers, what they look at first...) are drawn in child.py draw_habits().

habits: overrides one of the habits drawn in draw_habits() for this profile (e.g. pronouns, inserts = the stray words the recogniser adds). style: extra speech rules given to the child model for this profile only.

p_persist: probability that, after an animation it has seen, the child says the previous sentence again (an ASSUMPTION anchored on one child: P1 28%, P16 0%). Set for N5-N8 only; N1-N4 are left as last sampled.
echo_guard: when true, a recording that reuses phrases of the written scene description is written again, once (child.py echoes()). Set for N5-N8 only.
ignore_target: when true, a child who ignores an animation talks about something other than its target. Set for N5-N8 only.
labels: {story: {entity: word}} replaces the word drawn for a character (plainer than the app's own label).
picture_only: the child model gets the drawing and no written description (the child's words then come from the picture). N5-N8.
p_inner: probability that a recording is about what a character wants, thinks or feels, or what will happen (P16's register).
adult_specific: the adult next to the child talks about this very picture instead of using stock prompts.

profiles.label: N1
profiles.note: Independent narrator, short simple sentences; like P1 with slightly fewer errors.

habits.pronouns: names a character once per picture, then mixes the name and 'he', 'she' or 'they'

style: This child talks, and does not write: no 'as' or 'while' clause ('he waves as he walks off'), never two describing words in a row before a noun ('a big old boat'), a plain word for a place, never a dressed-up one, and no detail that only a caption would give (which hand, which way a window faces).

Each recording is built differently from this child's earlier ones in the story: not the same opening words, and no frame used twice (two recordings that both start 'They will probably', or both shaped 'X looks ... and ...').
A sentence joined with 'and' stays with one character or one event, never a feeling plus an unrelated detail. Most of this child's recordings name no feeling.

When this child puts something right after an animation, it is in a roundabout everyday way, a few plain words for what the character does or how it looks, never the one exact word an adult would pick.
Tells what is happening with 'is ...ing' or in the past ('is smiling', 'got it'), not in the plain present of a storybook ('smiles', 'gets', 'stands').
This child tells what happens, who does what to whom, and goes for the main event of the picture first: never what people wear or carry, never a posture, never where each thing stands.
Does not stress a place with 'right' ('right next to', 'right in the middle'): just 'next to', 'in the middle'.
Speech has short forms: 'doesn't', 'don't', 'isn't', 'can't'. Never 'does not', 'do not', 'is not', 'cannot'.

profiles.label: N2
profiles.note: Weak oral level, short simple sentences with bare verbs, and a parent talking next to the child, as for both real 8-year-olds (P2, P10), one notch milder than P2.
style: Speech has short forms: 'doesn't', 'don't', 'isn't', 'can't'. Never 'does not', 'do not', 'is not', 'cannot'.
Going on with the story, this child often starts a recording with 'And' or 'Then'.

style: This child talks, and does not write: no 'as' or 'while' clause ('he waves as he walks off'), never two describing words in a row before a noun ('a big old boat'), a plain word for a place, never a dressed-up one, and no detail that only a caption would give (which hand, which way a window faces).
